newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia ignores China warnings over Dalai Lama.
newsitem.headline: Australia ignores China warnings over Dalai Lama.

text.p: The Australian government made clear on Sunday it would not break contact with Tibet's exiled religious leader, the Dalai Lama, despite Chinese threats of damaged diplomatic relations.

Assistant Treasurer Jim Short, one of the government's economic ministers, was among 6,000 who welcomed the Dalai Lama at a Melbourne Buddhist celebration on Sunday, a day after he arrived in Sydney for a two-week Australian tour.
The Dalai Lama was "a very welcome visitor as a world spiritual leader," Short told reporters.

Organisers meanwhile announced that the Buddhist monk, exiled from his Chinese-controlled country since 1959, would attend a religious function in the ceremonial Great Hall of Parliament House in Canberra on Tuesday, when parliament will be in session.
The building also accommodates Prime Minister John Howard's government.
Chinese Premier Li Peng warned Australia last month against official contact with the Dalai Lama.
After New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger met the religious leader last week, Beijing said such official contact would damage New Zealand's relations with China.
Howard is not presently scheduled to meet the Dalai Lama, although the possibility of a meeting has not been ruled out.
But Australian Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer met the Dalai Lama on his arrival in Sydney on Saturday evening.
Downer had a meeting with the Dalai Lama but later said he and his wife had met him in his capacity as a religious leader and as private citizens.
China, insisting the Dalai Lama is leading a pro-independence cause, routinely objects to other states dealing with him.
